sampling_model.design: Known history-predictable randomization \(p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\) on ordered enrollment positions.
sampling_model.units: The typed unit-level potential-outcome schedule encodes no cross-unit interference, the observation map \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{bi}=Y_{bi}(Z_{bi})\) encodes consistency, block membership is fixed, and assignment is the experiment's only endogenous randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: The shared control is available in every block, while the focal arm has positive propensity exactly on the proper block window \(W\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every available arm has compatible-history propensity at least \(p_{\min}>0\); structural zeros off the availability set are allowed, and information is averaged under the induced assignment law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Outcome regressions \(m_{bi}(z)\) are bounded and predictable; validity does not require consistency of these regressions.
sampling_model.procedure_randomization: A schedule-independent Markov kernel may use an auxiliary \(U_{\mathrm{aux}}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) independent of the assignment experiment; coverage and expected length are computed under that same extended law. The concurrent-only subclass observes all assignment and realized propensity metadata but no outcome outside \(W\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The two-stage adding-arm simulations compare all-control and concurrent-only analyses under linear and step trends, and the stage-adjusted analysis is equivalent to concurrent-only analysis while linear adjustment can fail under nonlinear drift.

Equation (3) writes the two-period regression estimator as a concurrent-control mean plus a weighted nonconcurrent trend adjustment, and Section 3.1.2 gives unbiasedness under equal additive arm trends.

Theorem 3 gives the efficient influence function for the concurrent average treatment effect, and Section 6 finds no first-order doubly robust NCC efficiency gain when availability is deterministic in entry time.
Theorem 4 proves design-unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem for finite-population AIPW under adaptive randomization with positive propensity for every analyzed treatment.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 optimize honest confidence intervals through convex-class modulus and worst-case bias geometry in a Gaussian regression experiment.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds the expected length of every honest interval by a between-class Gaussian modulus and constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals over convex classes.
The paper selects data-adaptive external-control weights to keep estimated expected bias below a prespecified cap and reports bootstrap Wald inference under model-based assumptions.

Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction in a Gaussian RCT-plus-observational model with bounded scalar confounding bias; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility.

Definitions 2.1--2.3 define a concurrently randomized cohort by a common allocation design, define nonconcurrent controls by membership outside that cohort, and distinguish contemporaneous controls by same-stage enrollment.

The paper compares categorical fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline calendar-time adjustments for platform-trial nonconcurrent controls through simulation-based type-I-error and power analysis, finding spline control for sufficiently smooth trends and period fixed effects most robust for arbitrary equal-across-arm trends.

body.tldr: A cumulative-discrepancy linear program gives the exact worst-case bias from borrowing nonconcurrent controls, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope. Projection yields an everywhere-nonempty, uniformly design-honest interval whose worst-case expected length is at most twice the clipped optimized radius. For every adaptive design, every honest observed-data interval kernel also obeys the generic lower bound \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha)\). A masked-focal construction supplies an additional finite-tree computable lower certificate by locating target-weighted positions that the all-zero adaptive tree fails to assign to the focal arm with probability at least \(1-\eta_\alpha\). An explicit three-block rare-history sequence proves that no positive constant depending only on \(\alpha\) can lower-compare minimax expected length to the optimized AIPW radius over the unrestricted primitive class: the radius remains \(2M\) while an honest variable-length interval has expected length tending to zero. Thus the radius is a constructive upper scale, not a generic minimax characterization. The separate KKT certificate still determines strict improvement over the concurrent AIPW rule. At zero drift the convex program is purely information-optimal, while at vacuous drift the full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel values agree under the accepted structural invariance of propensities to off-window outcomes. The enumerated one-unit three-block experiment retains its certified zero-drift minimax value \(0.7M\); no positive-drift value is inferred from it.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers study parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work gives minimax expected-length theory in nonadaptive observation experiments. None supplies a fixed-schedule adaptive-randomization theorem that separates a universally honest predictable-AIPW upper radius from the smaller expected length attainable by variable-length intervals when severe propensities occur only on rare histories. The unrestricted alpha-only equivalence is therefore not merely absent from the literature; it is false.
project_justification.niche: The note treats the adaptive assignment tree as part of the experiment and keeps fixed potential outcomes distinct from assignment randomness. It combines the exact support function of the bounded-total-variation control-mean class with actual-history martingale information, an all-kernel observed-law mixture modulus, and an explicit finite-tree masked-focal testing certificate. This separates the causal finite-population contrast, an implementable honest AIPW radius, and the minimax expected length over all observed-data interval kernels.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is a sharp drift-bias dual, a convex-program projected interval with worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, a generic mixture-modulus lower bound for every schedule-independent randomized interval, a computable masked-history lower certificate, and an explicit rare-history impossibility for any unrestricted alpha-only radius comparison. The optimizer certificate characterizes strict gain over the concurrent AIPW rule rather than over the all-kernel minimax value. The accepted boundary results remain intact: zero drift removes the borrowing bias, and vacuous drift gives equality with the concurrent-only all-kernel benchmark only when propensity updates are structurally unchanged by off-window potential-outcome changes holding assignments and window outcomes fixed.

body.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift analyze all-control versus concurrent-only platform procedures under specified linear, step, fixed-effect, mixed-effect, or spline time models and emphasize bias, type-I error, and power. MarschnerSchou2024 defines concurrency through randomized cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies a superpopulation efficiency problem for the concurrent estimand. Those results motivate the platform setting but do not give uniform fixed-schedule coverage over a total-variation drift class or minimax expected length over schedule-independent observed-data kernels. LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template; here the information envelope averages under each schedule's actual adaptive assignment law, so a rare branch contributes through both its probability and its inverse propensity. ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 provide Gaussian bias--variance and mixture-modulus analogies, but their likelihood geometry does not justify a radius comparison after observed outcomes feed back into later assignments. The rare-history construction proves that an alpha-only comparison is false for the primitive adaptive class. The positive all-kernel statements are instead the generic observed-law modulus bound and the masked-focal certificate: two explicit bounded schedules coincide on a sufficiently probable zero-outcome subtree and have a computable target separation. No comparison of either lower object to the optimized AIPW radius is claimed. SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 selects external-control weights under an estimated bias cap, but its estimand, confounding model, bootstrap interval, and guarantee differ from the present fixed-population randomization result. AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 provide bounded finite-population minimax benchmarks without staggered availability, TV borrowing, or adaptive-history masking.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale but is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale. The counterexample exploits the distinction between a second-moment interval that pays for a rare low-propensity branch and a variable-length procedure that can spend part of its allowed miscoverage on that branch. Its sequence has a positive propensity floor in every experiment, but the floor decreases with the block-two sample size; whether additional independently motivated uniform reachability or fixed-floor restrictions yield a sharper radius comparison is not settled here. The masked-history expression is an exact, finite-tree computable lower certificate and lower-bounds the observed-law modulus construction by explicit testing schedules, but no comparison of it or the modulus to the optimized AIPW radius is asserted. The vacuous-drift reduction separately requires propensity invariance across schedules when only off-window outcomes change; mere predictability does not imply that invariance.
body.honest_scope: The causal target is the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the experiment's only source of randomness. The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest for every design satisfying the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions, with no regression-consistency or asymptotic-normality premise. The all-kernel mixture-modulus lower bound and the finite masked-focal testing certificate are also generic. No universal alpha-only equivalence between minimax expected length and the optimized AIPW radius is claimed: an explicit admissible three-block sequence refutes it while maintaining positivity in every experiment. The masked-focal result supplies a computable lower benchmark only; it is not used as a witness-form premise for any radius comparison. The KKT result compares NCC and concurrent-only AIPW radii, not the two all-kernel minimax values. At zero drift, equal control block means eliminate borrowing bias and leave the program to minimize assignment-law-averaged information; under the boundary proposition's nondegeneracy condition every block receives positive weight. At vacuous drift, full-record and concurrent-only all-kernel minimax values coincide only under the accepted structural condition that propensity updates are invariant to off-window potential-outcome changes with assignments and window outcomes fixed. The separate finite three-block LP asserts only its proved zero-drift value \(0.7M\), supported by matching primal and dual certificates. No claim is made that the drift budget is identified from trial data, that the masked certificate is necessary, or that the finite LP has the same value at positive drift.
